title: Anne Arundel Council approves 15-month data center moratorium
source_used: Capital Gazette page summary line (pool link; the article body did not load); WBAL News Radio's report of the same day before the vote
key_facts: The Capital Gazette and the Baltimore Sun (reporter Benjamin Rothstein) reported on 5 Oct 2026 that the Anne Arundel County Council in Maryland unanimously approved a moratorium on data center projects in the county.
The headline calls it a 15-month moratorium; the page's own summary line says 18 months.

WBAL News Radio reported before the vote that the council the week before had unanimously changed an outright ban into a moratorium lasting until 31 Jan 2028 or until the county adopts legislation to regulate data centers.
During the moratorium the council would set up a work group to study energy and water use, utility infrastructure, environmental impacts, air quality, noise and economic development.
The work group would then recommend regulations for the county to consider.
quote_evidence: The Anne Arundel County Council unanimously approved an 18-month moratorium on data center projects within the county.

Last week, the council unanimously approved a measure changing a ban on the facilities to a moratorium that would last until Jan. 31, 2028, or until the county adopts legislation on regulating the centers.
During the moratorium, the council would set up a work group to study energy and water use, utility infrastructure, environmental impacts, air quality, noise and economic development.
why_it_matters_hint: A Maryland county has paused new data center projects while a work group studies the effects and recommends rules.
notes: The Capital Gazette and Baltimore Sun articles did not load beyond their summary line; the details come from WBAL's report of the same day, written before the vote. The length is inconsistent in the Gazette's own page: the headline says 15 months, the summary line says 18; WBAL gives an end date of 31 Jan 2028 for the version before the vote. The Baltimore Sun carries the same article.
